data.long_meaning: Elumalai is a Tamil name derived from the Tamil words ‘Elu’ which means hill and ‘Malai’ which means mountain or hill. The name Elumalai is believed to be associated with Lord Subramanya or Murugan, who is the deity of hills and mountains. In Hindu mythology, Lord Subramanya is also known as Kartikeya or Skanda and is the son of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati. Elumalai is a revered name in Tamil Nadu and is often used to honor the divine presence of Lord Subramanya.

He was a devout Saivite and became a follower of Ramaswamy Ramalinga Swamy, who established the religion of Sri Ayyappan in South India. Elumalai joined the Sri Ayyappan movement and played a significant role in its development. He led several processions, organized religious festivals, and spread the message of the new religion. In 1872, he was arrested and imprisoned by the British authorities for his involvement in the movement. He was released in 1878 and continued his activities until his death in 1924.

His most famous work is the 'Tirumurai', a collection of 27 Tamil Saiva Agamas. He also wrote commentaries on the Agama texts and other works.
